title: Shallow-clone identity: refuse with remediation (D-4)
attempted: Pre-implementation verification of the T2 gate assumption ('eval repos are full clones') before writing any code, as the task contract required. It is false.
evidence: All 7 default eval repos are shallow: for r in ~/drift-falsification/repos/*/; do git -C $r rev-parse --is-shallow-repository; done -> true for calcom, dub, formbricks, midday, openstatus, papermark, taxonomy; git rev-list --count HEAD = 1 in every one (depth-1 clones, same as the repos-audit copies). scripts/external-eval.mjs:223 runs `drift start --repo-root .` inside each repo and scripts/evasion-matrix.mjs uses the same repo set. D-4 places the refusal in repoIdentityFor (packages/cli/src/domain/repo-identity.ts:97), the seam reached by start/scan/check/contract via repoRecordForRoot (repo-paths.ts:148) - so a correct X-1 makes every eval invocation exit 3 and the ENTIRE T2 suite (eval:external 7/7 + eval:evasion 91 cells) fails, not as a regression but as the refusal working as specified on a fixture set that lies about identity in exactly the way X-1 exists to refuse.
diagnosis: The conflict is between the pre-registered D-4 decision (refuse shallow at the shared identity seam) and the measurement substrate (the pinned eval repos are themselves depth-1 clones). Any resolution changes what the suite measures: (a) `git fetch --unshallow` in each eval repo keeps HEAD identical (verified: same tips) and makes fingerprints full-history root-commit based - the baseline pins NO fingerprint values (grep fingerprint scripts/external-eval-baseline.json -> 0 hits) so no baseline change is expected, but network + ~GBs of history for calcom et al are required and PROTOCOL.md warns that altering the pinned repos silently changes what the suite measures; (b) harness passes an --allow-shallow-identity escape hatch - weakens the suite so it never again exercises the default refusal path, and D-4 permits the flag only if it records absolute_path-grade non-portability, which would alter fingerprint semantics inside the suite; (c) exempting the harness some other way violates one-writer/hermeticity rules. Choosing among these is an orchestrator decision, not an implementer one.
needs: Orchestrator decision: unshallow the 7 eval repos (recommended: `git -C repos/<r> fetch --unshallow` preserves HEAD; re-verify eval:external is byte-stable before X-1 lands) OR pre-register a harness-level escape hatch. X-1 implementation itself is unblocked the moment the repos are full.

The glob primitives were never divergent: matchesPolicyGlob is already an alias for core's matchesGlob and apiCompatibleGlobs for expandApiRouteScopeGlobs. The divergence is that mcp/src/index.ts:2160 applies globs only and never consults exclude_path_globs, so an explicitly excluded file is still reported 'in scope for <convention_id>' on the agent-facing relevant_files surface and inherits that convention's roles.
needs: A decision. It looks like a bug rather than a policy: MCP's own sibling scopeMatchesFile (:2461) does honour exclusions, so one file disagrees with itself. Impact is bounded - default onboarding writes exclude_path_globs: [], so it is latent until an author narrows their contract, and it mislabels a packet rather than weakening enforcement, which goes through the core predicate. Recommendation: treat as a bug and route :2160 through conventionScopeFiles. Committed as a differential test with the divergence pinned as a KNOWN DEFECT, so the fix will fail that test on purpose.
